sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Jenkins interview questions cover the CI server still running half the world's Java backend pipelines — declarative vs scripted pipelines, Jenkinsfile structure, agents, shared libraries, credentials and secrets, plugin ecosystem, multi-branch pipelines, and the upgrade-and-stability concerns that come up in interviews for Jenkins-heavy shops. For broader CI/CD comparisons (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI), see the CI/CD page.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
Jenkins = **a job orchestrator** with a pipeline DSL.

- **Declarative pipeline** = recommended; **scripted** = full Groovy.
- **Agents** — controllers shouldn't run jobs; pin agents by label.
- **Shared libraries** — code reuse across `Jenkinsfile`s.
- **Credentials** — bound at step level; never echoed.
- **Multi-branch** — auto-discovers branches, builds PRs.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
The interview surface for this module breaks into these focus areas:

- **Jenkins pipelines** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **Don't run on the controller** — security + scaling.
- **Plugins are the failure surface** — pin versions, treat as code.
- **Pipeline parallelism** — `parallel { ... }` block; quick win for slow tests.
- **Stash / unstash** — workspace handoff between agents.
- **Migration off Jenkins** is common; but legacy hosts make it sticky.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"I'd run declarative pipelines with versioned shared libraries, pin agents by label, scope credentials per-step, and treat plugin upgrades as code review. For new shops I'd consider GitHub Actions or GitLab CI before standing up Jenkins."*
